title: Caring for Silk and Lace Between Wears
excerpt: Occasion fabrics are the most fragile things in most wardrobes — and the most expensive to get wrong. Here's how to keep them intact.
author: Lipek Fashion Team
body: Silk should never be left balled up in a bag after wear, even overnight. Hang it on a padded hanger as soon as possible to let any creasing from sitting or movement relax out naturally.
Avoid direct sunlight for extended storage — silk and lace both fade and weaken with prolonged UV exposure, which is why we recommend breathable garment bags over clear plastic ones.

Spot-clean stains immediately with a dry cloth rather than rubbing with water, which can set certain dyes. For anything beyond a light mark, bring it to us rather than attempting a home fix — lace and beading are easy to damage with the wrong solvent.
Store beaded or embroidered pieces flat when possible. Hanging heavy beadwork for long periods can stretch the fabric it's sewn onto.
